en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Sixth Chapter
Discussion on the Attainment of Cessation:
Is the attainment of cessation unconditioned? Yes.
“Is Nibbāna a refuge, a shelter, a resort, a final goal, the undecaying, the deathless?
“One must not say so.
… [as before] … “Is the attainment of cessation unconditioned? Is Nibbāna unconditioned?”
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there two unconditioned things?
You should not say so …pe…
Are there two unconditioned things?
Yes. Are there two refuges? ... [and so on] ...
Does the intermediate space blow?
One should not say so… [as before] … Is the attainment of cessation unconditioned?
“Yes.
“Is it the case that some enter into cessation, acquire it, produce it, co-produce it, bring it forth, co-bring it forth, generate it, co-generate it, cause it to arise, and co-cause it to arise?
“Yes.”
Is it the case that some enter into, obtain, produce, co-produce, arouse, co-arouse, generate, co-generate, bring forth, or fully bring forth the unconditioned?
You should not say so… [etc.
… Is purification and emergence from cessation discernible?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is purification and emergence manifested as unconditioned?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is it the case that for one entering the attainment of cessation, first the verbal formation ceases, then the bodily formation, and then the mental formation?
Yes. Is it the case that for one entering the unconditioned, first the verbal formation ceases, then the bodily formation, and then the mental formation?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … For one emerging from cessation, does the mental formation arise first, then the bodily formation, and then the verbal formation? Yes.
Is it the case that for one emerging from the unconditioned, first the mental formation arises, then the bodily formation, and then the verbal formation?
One should not say so… [etc.
…Three types of contact touch one who has emerged from cessation:
Is there contact that is empty, contact that is signless, and contact that is desireless?
Yes. Do these three contacts touch one who has emerged from the unconditioned? Yes.
“Is there contact that is empty, contact that is signless, and contact that is desireless?
“One should not say so…” [and so on].
“Does the mind of one who has emerged from cessation tend toward seclusion, incline toward seclusion, and lean toward seclusion?”
“Yes,” you say.
“Is the mind of one who has emerged from the unconditioned inclined toward seclusion, sloping toward seclusion, and leaning toward seclusion?
You should not say so… [and so on].
Is it not to be said that the attainment of cessation is unconditioned?
Yes, it is.
"Is it conditioned?
"One should not say so...
[and so on] "...therefore, the attainment of cessation is unconditioned."
The Discussion on the Attainment of Cessation is finished.
